notBuiltYet: This one is not built yet. It is named here because it is a promise, not a placeholder — when it opens, it opens from this page.

social.name: Pana Social
social.headline:
A Feed
That Is Ours
social.lede: A local social network that federates, so the community owns its own timeline instead of renting one from a company that sells it back.

one.title: Post to the block
one.body: Text, photos and voice notes, seen by the panas who follow you — in the order they were posted, never in the order an ad system would prefer.

two.title: Federated by default
two.body: Pana Social speaks ActivityPub, so your posts reach Mastodon and the rest of the fediverse, and your handle stays yours if you ever leave.

three.title: Built on the directory
three.body: The people in your feed are the same creatives, organizations and small businesses listed in the directory. Neighbors, not strangers.

closing.lede: Every other timeline you read belongs to someone whose business is selling your attention back to you. This one belongs to the people in it.

directory.name: Directory
directory.headline:
Find Your
People
directory.lede: South Florida's living archive of the creatives, entrepreneurs and small businesses who make this place what it is — searchable by name, category and neighborhood.

one.title: Search like you mean it
one.body: Keyword, category, county and distance. "Support local" stops being a slogan the moment you can act on it by name.

two.title: Three counties, one map
two.body: Broward, Miami-Dade and Palm Beach. Everyone listed lives or works here — that is the whole of the eligibility rule.

three.title: Your listing, your words
three.body: Claim a listing or start one from scratch, and describe what you do yourself rather than leaving it to a review site.

closing.lede: The directory exists so that the next time you need something, the answer is a neighbor with a name rather than whoever paid the most for the top of the page.

events.name: Events
events.headline:
Show Up
Somewhere
events.lede: Markets, workshops, art builds and long dinners across South Florida — co-hosted with the people already doing the work.

one.title: Gatherings, not networking
one.body: Events built for real connection rather than for handing out cards: dinners, markets, workshops and nights out worth staying at.

two.title: Host your own
two.body: Any pana can put something on the calendar, take RSVPs and run the door. You do not need a venue or a budget to start.

three.title: All three counties
three.body: See what is happening near you this week, or find the one that is worth the drive up or down the coast.

closing.lede: A directory tells you who is out there. An event is where you actually meet them. Come to one, then host the next.

vizion.name: PanaVizión
vizion.headline:
Local, On
The Record
vizion.lede: Conversations with the people building South Florida's local economy, in their own voices and at their own length.

one.title: The podcast
one.body: Long-form conversations with panas about the work, the setbacks, and what it actually takes to build something here.

two.title: An archive, not a feed
two.body: Every episode stays up and stays findable long after the week it aired, because the point is the record rather than the release.

three.title: Bring your own mic
three.body: Panas get pitched, featured and interviewed. If you are doing the work, we want it on the record in your own words.

closing.lede: Who gets recorded is who gets remembered. PanaVizión exists so that the people holding South Florida together are in the archive, not just in the traffic.

ink.name: Pana Ink Press
ink.headline:
Words You
Can Hand Over
ink.lede: Zines, pamphlets and print that explain the local movement in a form anyone can pass to anyone — no login, no algorithm, no battery.

one.title: Zines and pamphlets
one.body: Short print runs made with local artists and writers, designed to be given away rather than sold.

two.title: The dispatches
two.body: Longer reads from the people building South Florida's local economy. These are already published on the site while the press gets going.

three.title: Print as infrastructure
three.body: Paper keeps working when a platform changes its mind. That is the whole argument for a community having a press of its own.

closing.lede: A zine handed to someone at a market reaches further than a post does, and it is still there next year. The press is how the movement travels off the screen.

getInvolved.name: Get Involved
getInvolved.headline:
Start Where
You Are
getInvolved.lede: Pana MIA is built by the people in it. There is a way in whatever you have to give — an hour, a skill, a room, or a few dollars a month.

one.title: Become a Pana
one.body: Join the directory so your neighbors can find you, and so the club has one more local name standing behind it.

two.title: Community Connectors
two.body: Pods across Miami-Dade, Broward and Palm Beach running projects for their own neighborhoods. Three tiers of involvement, and everyone starts at tier one.

three.title: Keep it running
three.body: The directory, the feed and the events are paid for by members and donations rather than by selling anybody's attention.

closing.lede: Pana MIA was started so that anyone with an idea for making South Florida better had somewhere to bring it. Bring yours.
